content:
nisha: Heads-up — planning a small, non-disruptive traffic nudge from na-edge-primary -> na-edge-secondary tomorrow 2026-03-18 10:00 PDT. Plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over ~30m if metrics look good. Goal is validation of weighted-route behavior and cold-cache perf for a subset of low-latency customers. Who can own smoke checks + rollback readiness?

kevin: I can own smoke. I’ll be on hand at +1 (10:00 PDT). What’s the exact command we’ll use to flip weights? Are we using weighted DNS or LB policy change?

nisha: good q — this will be a weighted routing policy change in our route-orch (not DNS TTL). We'll update route weights in the control plane: change policy na-edge/primary weight from 80 -> 55 -> 30 -> 0 while setting secondary to 20 -> 45 -> 70 -> 100. deploy-bot preflight should run first.

deploy-bot: preflight checks passed for na-edge policy update (config syntax, auth, capacity quotas). Run ID: run_20260318_1000

kevin: smoke checklist (short):
- run quick health checks against 3 vantage points
- validate p50/p95 latency on edge-routes dashboard
- watch 5xx/error rate on api-gateway
- confirm KV cache hit % not dropping >10%

kevin: quick commands I'll run:
```
# from ci/ops box
curl -sS -H "Host: test-lowlat.example.com" https://na-edge-secondary.example.com/health
curl -I -H "Host: test-lowlat.example.com" https://na-edge-secondary.example.com/ | grep -i x-cache
``` 

ops-oncall: I’ll be the escalation during the window (oncall: @maria). If anything >5% error spike or latency p95 > 1s we abort and rollback.

irene: TTL note — control-plane routing takes effect immediately. No need to wait for DNS. But we should keep a 5m quiet-window after each step to observe metrics. Also confirm tracing headers are present so we can backtrace slow requests.

maria: Re: rollback plan — simplest rollback is to reapply previous policy snapshot (route-orch rollback) which sets weights back. Script available:
```
./tools/route-orch apply-snapshot --snapshot=na-edge-20260316 --run-id=roll_$(date +%s)
``` 
Also have manual button in the console if we need instant revert.

kevin: I'll validate the rollback script beforehand and run a dry-run now. Also will pin a small subset of sessions to the secondary pool for a smoke cohort: header X-Smoke-Cohort: na-edge-smoke

nisha: OK can we also add a quick canary for customer-corp-id 42? maria — can you confirm that corp-42 traffic is routed through the test host so we can assert functional correctness before wider ramp?

maria: confirmed — corp-42 test bucket is ready. I’ll seed 100 requests at each step after weight change and report pass/fail.

kevin: monitoring targets to watch (dash links pasted):
- Grafana: edge.routes.latency (p50/p95)
- Grafana: edge.routes.errors (5xx count)
- Prometheus: na_edge_kv_cache_hit_ratio
- Sentry: service-failure spikes

irene: small gotcha — if cache warmup causes initial latency blips, treat them as expected for first 10 minutes but watch error rates closely.

nisha: timeline recap:
- 09:55 PDT — final preflight and deploy-bot check
- 10:00 PDT — step1 5% -> 5% (really just ensure control path ok)
- 10:05 PDT — step2 25%
- 10:15 PDT — step3 50%
- 10:30 PDT — final 100% (if green)

kevin: ack. I’ll post live status in this thread with short notes after each step and a final summary. If anything goes red I’ll run the rollback script and post the run id.

nisha: thanks all. small ask — please make sure you have console access and paging enabled. I’ll update the calendar invite with the run id and add the runbook link.

kevin: ready. :thumbsup:

maria: ready. I'll seed corp-42 and report results after each step.

deploy-bot: scheduled run run_20260318_1000 -> queued. Notifying ops-oncall.

nisha: perfect — see you tomorrow. If anyone needs to opt-out ping me here.
